headline: MIT researchers used an AI system to find an mRNA vaccine formulation that stayed fully active for over two months at 37 degrees Celsius, in animal tests.
score_reason: Promising but animal-stage work published 28 Sep and reported weeks later; one point below the pool score.
importance_line: Vaccines that do not need deep freezing could reach places without cold storage, but the results are from mice and macaques and human safety and effectiveness are untested.
summary: Reuters reports, as relayed by DongA Science, that an MIT team used an AI agent that suggests the next experiment to find a solid vaccine formulation that kept full biological activity after more than two months at 37 degrees Celsius, with results published on 28 Sep 2026 in Nature Biotechnology. Stored vaccines produced immune responses comparable to existing ones in mice and macaques, and the team expects storage and transport savings of up to 86 percent, but safety and effectiveness in people have not been tested.
notes: Read at DongA Science, which credits Reuters (7 Oct) for the report on the 28 Sep paper; Reuters itself not opened. v1 category HEA (vaccine) rather than the RES default.
